wga:zearly/1/2mural/2marcell/marcel11.summary: On the ceiling of a burial chamber, Christ sits enthroned at the centre, bearded and haloed, in a dark robe with an open book, while Peter and Paul stand on either side gesturing toward him. In the register below, the Lamb stands on a hill, and four martyrs of this catacomb, labelled with their names, approach in acclamation. The painting joins the heavenly court of Christ with the local saints venerated in this very place.
facts: The four martyrs below are named by painted inscriptions; the names of Gorgonius and Tiburtius can still be partly read, and the group is usually completed by Peter and Marcellinus, the martyrs after whom the catacomb is named.
The Lamb standing on a mount, the symbol of Christ sacrificed and victorious, is a motif that later reappears in the apse mosaics of Roman churches.

wga:zearly/1/2mural/2marcell/marcel11.notes: The identification of all four martyrs is based on the usual reading of this fresco; only parts of the inscriptions are legible in the photograph. Some scholars date the painting to the late 4th or early 5th century.
